pairs.why: A's anchor has clean, smooth contours with soft rim highlights like the real cards, while B has scratchy nicks and extra fine edge marks on the body.
B's cooler has clean, even edges with no surface scratches, while A has scuff lines on the front face that add edges the real cards lack.
B has only one thin crack line and a smooth rounded contour, while A's jagged chip on the top corner adds a busy broken edge the real cards do not have.
A's locker has thick, soft, rounded louvres and edges similar to the real card, while B's thinner, sharper panel lines and more precise hinges read as drawn linework.
Both have similar crisp body edges and streaky airflow, so edges give no reason to choose.
A keeps a calm background with few edges around the pump like the real card, while B adds a barrel, rocks and spiky bushes that raise background edge density.
B has a softer focus falloff and fewer hard-edged parts, like the real card's soft truss and lamp, while A's barn doors and boxy truss add many crisp edges.
B's rover is simpler, with softer large forms and fewer small edges such as vents and tread blocks, closer to the real cards' clean shapes.
